Kurt Vincent Thomas was born on October 4, 1972.
Kurt Thomas is an American former professional basketball player.
Kurt Thomas's height is 6'9".
Kurt Thomas weighs 230 lb.
Kurt Thomas played as a power forward-center in the NBA.
Kurt Thomas had a hard-nosed playing style and tough defense during his career.
Kurt Thomas played college basketball at Texas Christian University.
Kurt Thomas was drafted by the Miami Heat in 1995.
Kurt Thomas played parts of 18 seasons in the NBA.
Kurt began his basketball career on the playgrounds at Dallas Birdie Alexander Elementary.
Kurt continued his basketball career at D.A. Hulcy Middle School.
Kurt then played for Dallas Carter High.
Kurt transferred to Hillcrest High.
Kurt grew up in Dallas.

Kurt Thomas led the NCAA Division I in scoring and rebounding in the 1994–95 season with 28.9 PPG and 14.6 RPG.
Kurt Thomas became only the third player in history to lead the NCAA Division I in both scoring and rebounding (the other two being Hank Gathers and Xavier McDaniel).
Kurt Thomas began his NBA career with the Miami Heat from 1995 to 1997.
In Kurt's rookie season, he started 42 of his 74 games played.
On December 10, 1995, Kurt set a then career high with 29 points and grabbed 15 rebounds in a loss to the Sacramento Kings.
The following season, Kurt only played 18 games before suffering a stress fracture in his right ankle which required surgery.
During his rehab, Kurt Thomas, along with Sasha Danilović and Martin Müürsepp, were traded to the Dallas Mavericks for Jamal Mashburn.
Kurt's playing career with Dallas was short; he only played 5 games before suffering another stress fracture in the same ankle.
This placed him on the injured list for the remainder of the season.
Then-coach and general manager Don Nelson hired Kurt as an assistant coach during his rehab.
In the offseason, Kurt Thomas decided to become a free agent and signed with the New York Knicks.
Kurt played seven seasons with the New York Knicks from 1999 to 2005.
During this time, the team went to the playoffs four times.
The New York Knicks included two trips to the Eastern Conference Finals (1999 and 2000) and one trip to the NBA Finals (1999).
On March 28, 1999, Kurt was disqualified and fined $5,000 for a flagrant foul against Dennis Rodman during a 99-91 loss against the Los Angeles Lakers.
In the 2001 NBA Playoffs, Kurt averaged 14.4 points and 11.2 rebounds while starting all five games in a 2-3 first round series loss against the Toronto Raptors.
Kurt's best personal success perhaps came in the 2001-02 NBA season, where he started all 82 regular season games and averaged 13.2 points and 9.1 rebounds per game.
During this season, Kurt scored a career high 33 points on March 17, 2002.
Kurt also scored a career high 33 points on November 8, 2002.
Kurt Thomas played two seasons with the Phoenix Suns from 2005 to 2007.

On July 20, 2007, Kurt, along with the Suns' first-round draft choices in 2008 and 2010 (which became Serge Ibaka and Quincy Pondexter), was traded by the Suns to the Seattle SuperSonics in exchange for a conditional second-round draft choice and an $8 million trade exception.
Kurt Thomas was traded by the Sonics to the San Antonio Spurs on February 20, 2008, for Francisco Elson, Brent Barry, and a 2009 first-round draft pick.
Kurt with the Milwaukee Bucks On June 23, 2009, Kurt was traded along with Bruce Bowen and Fabricio Oberto to the Milwaukee Bucks for Richard Jefferson.
On July 26, 2010, the Chicago Bulls signed Kurt Thomas.
Because of injuries to the Bulls' starting center Joakim Noah and power forward Carlos Boozer, Kurt Thomas saw some significant playing time, including 37 starts.
When Noah and Boozer came back, Kurt experienced minimal playing time with Ömer Aşık playing in front of him on the bench.

Although his playing time was slim during this span, Kurt Thomas won the appeal of Chicago fans with some emphatic highlights which were referred to as "Turning back the Clock" and eventually earned him the nickname "Big Sexy".
Thomas averaged more than 20 minutes per game during the 2010-11 season along with 4.1 points and 5.8 rebounds.
On December 11, 2011, the Portland Trail Blazers signed Kurt Thomas for the shortened 2011-2012 season.
Though terms for the deal were not disclosed officially, it was reported to be a two-year contract.
On July 16, 2012, Kurt and Raymond Felton were traded to the New York Knicks for Jared Jeffries, Dan Gadzuric, the rights to Kostas Papanikolaou and Giorgos Printezis, and a second round draft pick.
On April 12, 2013, the Knicks waived Thomas.
